meta.title: Safety First in the Experiment Room

paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers visited the science museum. Guide Ann met them at the door of the Experiment Room. A big sign was next to the door, and it had a picture for each step. "Please read the sign first," said Guide Ann. "Safety is the most important thing in an experiment." Lily read the sign slowly, and Mia took a photo of it. "Why does the sign have a picture for each step?" asked Mia. "A picture helps everybody to understand fast," said Guide Ann.

This is what the sign said. "SAFETY FIRST" "One: Wear safety glasses in this room." "Two: Do not eat or drink here." "Three: Listen to Guide Ann before you start." "Four: Danger! Do not touch the hot water." "Five: Children aged under ten need an adult." "Six: Wash your hands afterwards." "I like number four," said Leo, "because it has a red picture."

Then Guide Ann showed them a big drum. She put a little rice on top of the drum. "Now hit the drum with this wooden spoon," she said to Mia. Mia put on safety glasses and hit the drum, but not hard. The rice jumped into the air! "That is amazing!" said May. "The drum shakes when you hit it, and the shaking moves the rice," said Guide Ann.

Leo wanted to try, too, and he moved very fast. His arm hit a glass on the table. Luckily, the glass was empty, and it did not break. "Walk slowly in this room," said Guide Ann, "and look before you move." She showed them a box on the wall with a red cross. "This box has a bandage for a small cut," she said. "For more medicine, there is a pharmacy across the road."

Each child made the rice jump two times, and everybody was careful. Lily wrote the six steps in her notebook, and she drew a small picture for each step. "Safety signs help everybody," she said. "Yes," said Guide Ann, "and they help most when you listen to them." At the end, the children washed their hands. Leo smiled and said, "Now I know all six steps."
